answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 210 answers need 210 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the anchor index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the lantern audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the forge identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator pays for 210 runs and collects one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
